label: Services
gaps: Continue converting long-tail indexed services into field-by-field verified transaction guides.

label: Government service offices
gaps: Office moves and contact changes require continuing source-watch review.

label: Government
gaps: Department-level service and contact depth remains uneven outside the dedicated services directory.

label: Barangays
gaps: Locally published service information is now available on 18 of 23 barangay homepages through barangay service portals or current accredited health-facility records. Dasmariñas, Forbes Park, Magallanes, Urdaneta and Valenzuela still rely on the common transaction layer where no comparable current barangay-specific service source has been verified.
Email, standalone website and official social-channel coverage remains uneven; those completeness metrics are kept in the audit/status layer rather than promoted on the barangay gateway.

label: Elections
gaps: The 2025 barangay mayoral layer identifies which candidate carried all 23 current Makati barangays, but exact vote pairs are currently verified for only San Lorenzo and Guadalupe Nuevo.
Barangay-level 2025 totals for vice mayor, House and council races are not yet normalized.

The 2026 BSKE candidate directory is intentionally pending because certificate-of-candidacy filing opens on September 28, 2026 and BetterMakati will not infer a candidate list before an official COMELEC source exists.
Older mayoral elections use academic, mixed or archival-secondary sources where a stable official digital result table is unavailable; those source-quality limits are displayed with the records.

label: Projects & budget
gaps: The 21 structured procurement records have current follow-up checks; many awards still lack a separately published contract, notice to proceed, implementation or completion source.

The 2017–2018 audit findings have dated follow-up traces, but no official item-level COA closure table has been located for those specific recommendations; the 2024 SEF compliance report body is indexed but not retrievable through the current public download path.

label: History
gaps: The chronology is intentionally growing and does not claim exhaustive historical coverage.

label: Mobility
gaps: Operator schedules remain external and time-sensitive.

label: Today in Makati
gaps: Weather, news and published civic feeds depend on upstream availability and can refresh at different times.
Barangay context is currently a browser-saved preference; it does not infer or require the user's precise location.
Today surfaces the latest published Civic Brief and City Monitor status but does not treat raw news headlines or source-change signals as validated government activity.

label: Live Makati
gaps: Open-Meteo weather and air-quality readings are third-party observations; PAGASA remains the controlling source for official warnings.
Only city sources already covered by City Monitor receive a published BetterMakati check status. Utility, district and hazard links are direct handoffs unless separately monitored.
A source being reachable does not establish that no new advisory, outage or incident exists; users are routed to the original provider for current operational status.

label: City Monitor
gaps: No reliable current source has yet been normalized for every 2026 City Council session date, agenda, attendance, vote and minutes record.
The official legislation archive establishes enacted measures but does not yet expose a complete filing-to-effectivity lifecycle as structured data.

The Makati portal's news, events and speech collection pages are dynamically rendered, so the automated monitor treats them as reachability/discovery channels rather than claiming reliable content-change detection.
There is no single official current project-status feed or normalized publication feed covering all city projects and publications.
A detected source change still requires editorial verification before BetterMakati publishes it as a substantive civic record.

label: Civic Briefs
gaps: The archive begins on 24 September 2026; earlier daily/weekly/monthly briefs were not backdated or fabricated.
A brief can only be as current as the permanent City Monitor records that have passed editorial verification; raw source-change signals remain outside validated brief content.
Barangay relevance is shown only when a permanent City Monitor record has an explicit barangay tag; citywide records remain visible in a barangay view.
Automated publication creates website/RSS snapshots and share-ready copy, but it does not automatically post to BetterMakati social accounts.

label: Accountability Ledger
gaps: Procurement coverage is structured for the bid-result records already ingested, but many awards still lack a separately linked contract, notice to proceed, implementation or completion record.

The 2017–2018 Makati findings now carry dated follow-up traces, but the exact COA-validated closure status of those recommendations is not exposed in the retrievable public records; the 2024 SEF compliance report is indexed but its finding-level body remains unavailable through the current public download path.
Public commitments are source-backed but still selective rather than a comprehensive inventory of promises and measurable targets across speeches, plans, ordinances and announcements.
Barangay accountability now uses only explicit local tags and never falls back to citywide records, but fiscal, procurement and project evidence remains sparse for many of the 23 barangays.

label: Public Records
gaps: The catalog normalizes source URLs already used across BetterMakati; it is not yet an exhaustive inventory of every Makati public document published by every office.
A successful reachability check establishes that a dynamic portal responded; it does not prove that the portal's substantive content is unchanged.
Stable-document hash changes and failed checks are review signals. BetterMakati does not automatically rewrite site claims from a machine-detected change.
Barangay budgets, procurement, ordinances, resolutions and project records remain uneven across the 23 barangays.

label: Participation
gaps: Response time and participation conversion are not yet measured longitudinally.

label: Civic Map
gaps: Pilot asset coverage is intentionally small; verified public-transport route/stop objects still need expansion.
Referral lifecycle events can now be recorded, but delivery to government remains intentionally human-reviewed rather than automatic.

label: BetterMakati Status
gaps: Live status cards depend on published machine-readable feeds and display an unavailable state when an upstream feed cannot be read.
Source freshness reports monitoring health and review signals; it does not imply that every public record used by BetterMakati is in the automated watchlist.
